slides.title: Fill a moka pot the right way
slides.subtitle: Four small moves that change your morning coffee.

slides.myth: You should tamp the coffee down hard.
slides.truth: Not in a moka pot: just level it. Packed coffee makes it hard for water to pass, and the result tastes bitter and burnt.

slides.title: Filling it, in order
steps: Water in the bottom chamber, just below the valve.
Coffee in the filter basket, no tamping.
Level it and wipe stray grounds off the rim.
Screw it shut firmly, without forcing it.

slides.title: Why the valve matters
slides.body: It releases pressure if something gets blocked. If the water covers it, it can't do its job.
slides.highlight: Keep the water below the valve.

slides.caption: Roughly the pressure inside a moka pot. Espresso uses around 9: that's why they're two different coffees.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Low heat, and never let the flame reach past the sides of the base.

slides.title: Save it for tomorrow morning
slides.body: Four moves, no extra gear. The moka does the rest.
